subject: Geography
sub_topic: Census data — literacy, sex ratio, density

concepts.name: Definition and Methodology of Literacy Rate in Indian Census
key_dimensions: Census definition: persons aged 7+ who can read and write with understanding — exclusion of age 0-6 from denominator
Trap: Effective Literacy Rate vs. Crude Literacy Rate — which denominator is used officially
Historical shift in definition (pre-1991 vs post-1991 census methodology)
Why children below 7 are excluded — policy implications for NEP and RTE comparisons

concepts.name: State-wise Literacy Extremes and Patterns (Census 2011)
key_dimensions: Highest: Kerala (94%); Lowest: Bihar (61.8%) — exact figures frequently tested
Trap: Lakshadweep (92.28%) vs Kerala among UTs and states — category confusion
North-South literacy divide and its correlation with HDI, MMR, TFR
Male-Female literacy gap by state — states where gap is minimal vs maximal (Rajasthan has largest gender gap)

concepts.name: Gender Gap in Literacy: Female Literacy Rate Trends
key_dimensions: National female literacy (2011): 65.46% vs male: 82.14% — gap of ~16.68 percentage points
Fastest-improving states vs persistently low states (Rajasthan, UP, Bihar triangle)
Correlation with child marriage, MMR, fertility rate — interlinkages UPSC tests in GS1
BIMARU states pattern and implications for demographic dividend

concepts.name: Sex Ratio: Overall vs Child Sex Ratio — Definitional Distinction
key_dimensions: Overall Sex Ratio (2011): 943 females per 1000 males — definition and unit
Child Sex Ratio (0-6 years): 919 per 1000 — declining trend from 927 (2001) is a major trap
Trap: Child Sex Ratio declining even as overall sex ratio improves — paradox explanation
Policy response: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao — launched in Panipat, Haryana (worst CSR district)

concepts.name: State-wise Sex Ratio Extremes and Anomalies
key_dimensions: Highest overall sex ratio: Kerala (1084); Lowest: Haryana (879) — 2011 data
Trap: Among UTs — Puducherry has highest sex ratio (1037); Daman & Diu lowest (618) due to migrant male workers
Kerala paradox: high sex ratio explained by male out-migration, matrilineal traditions, high female education
States with sex ratio above 1000 (Kerala, Chhattisgarh, Manipur, Tamil Nadu) — frequently confused

concepts.name: Child Sex Ratio (0-6): Regional Patterns and Decline
key_dimensions: Worst child sex ratio states: Haryana (834), Punjab (846), J&K (862) — prosperous states performing poorly
Best child sex ratio: Mizoram (971), Meghalaya (970) — NE states and matrilineal societies
Trap: Economic prosperity vs CSR — inverse relationship in Punjab/Haryana contradicts development assumption
Technology-enabled sex-selective abortion post-1990s ultrasound proliferation — PCPNDT Act linkage

concepts.name: Population Density: Definition, Formula, and National Average
key_dimensions: Definition: persons per square kilometre — India's density: 382 persons/sq km (2011)
Trap: Density is NOT uniform — range from 17,900 in Delhi to 17 in Arunachal Pradesh
Decadal change in density — how to calculate and interpret
Density vs. Physiological Density vs. Agricultural Density — conceptual distinctions

concepts.name: State-wise Population Density Extremes
key_dimensions: Highest density state: Bihar (1106 per sq km) — NOT Delhi (which is a UT)
Trap: Highest density UT is Delhi (11,320) — state vs UT distinction critical
Lowest density state: Arunachal Pradesh (17 per sq km); Lowest UT: Andaman & Nicobar (46)
West Bengal among top dense states despite not being smallest — area-population interplay

concepts.name: Decadal Population Growth Rate Trends (2001–2011)
key_dimensions: National decadal growth rate (2001-2011): 17.7% — decline from 21.5% (1991-2001)
Fastest growing state: Meghalaya (27.9%); Slowest/Negative: Nagaland (-0.6%) — trap on NE states
Southern states achieving replacement-level fertility vs Northern states still growing fast
Implications of declining growth rate for demographic dividend window (2020-2040)

concepts.name: Demographic Dividend: Literacy and Sex Ratio as Enabling Conditions
key_dimensions: Definition: working-age population (15-64) bulge — India's window vs aging China/Europe
Role of female literacy in reducing TFR — Kerala model replicability
Trap: Demographic dividend is not automatic — requires health, education, employment trifecta
BIMARU states delaying national demographic transition — regional divergence in dividend realization

concepts.name: Urban Agglomeration vs Statutory Town vs Census Town — Census Definitions
key_dimensions: Census Town criteria: population ≥5000, density ≥400/sq km, 75%+ male workforce in non-agriculture
Statutory Town: declared by state government/municipality — political vs functional definition
Urban Agglomeration: continuous urban spread including outgrowths — Delhi UA vs Delhi city difference
Trap: Census 2011 showed sharp rise in Census Towns (3894) — reclassification inflating urbanization rate

concepts.name: Urbanization Rate in India: Levels, Trends, and Comparisons
key_dimensions: Urban population 2011: 31.16% — first census where absolute urban addition exceeded rural addition
Trap: India is still predominantly rural at ~69% — misquoting urbanization as majority
Most urbanized state: Goa (62.2%); Least: Himachal Pradesh (10%) among states
UT trap: Delhi (97.5%) and Chandigarh (97.25%) near fully urban — not comparable to states

concepts.name: Million-Plus Cities: Distribution and Growth (Census 2011)
key_dimensions: 53 million-plus cities in 2011 vs 35 in 2001 — significant jump
Four metro cities (Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai) vs emerging metros (Hyderabad, Bengaluru)
Delhi surpassing Mumbai as largest urban agglomeration — 2011 data
Primacy Index: Mumbai vs Delhi — UPSC sometimes tests urban primacy concept with Indian data

concepts.name: Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Distribution — Census Literacy and Sex Ratio Overlaps
key_dimensions: SC population: 16.6% of total; ST population: 8.6% — 2011 figures
Trap: SC literacy (66.1%) vs ST literacy (59%) vs national (74%) — different baselines
ST sex ratio (990) higher than national average (943) — tribal societies more gender equal in some metrics
States with highest ST population: MP, Maharashtra, Odisha vs states with highest ST percentage: Mizoram, Nagaland

concepts.name: Rural-Urban Literacy Differential and Its Policy Implications
key_dimensions: Rural literacy (2011): 67.8% vs Urban literacy: 84.1% — 16-point gap
Rural female literacy especially low — targeted by Saakshar Bharat Mission
Trap: High urban literacy masking low overall state literacy in highly urbanized but small states
Digital literacy vs functional literacy — emerging distinction in post-2011 policy discourse

concepts.name: Population Distribution: Physiographic and Climatic Determinants
key_dimensions: Indo-Gangetic Plain: 40%+ population on ~25% of area — most populated physiographic zone
Deccan Plateau moderate density vs Himalayan/Desert/Forest zones sparse — pattern reasoning
Trap: Highest density doesn't always mean highest absolute population — area multiplier effect
River valley civilization logic applied to modern density — Ganga-Yamuna doab, Brahmaputra valley

concepts.name: Sex Ratio at Birth vs Recorded Sex Ratio — Measurement Gaps
key_dimensions: Biological sex ratio at birth globally: ~105 males per 100 females (952 females per 1000 males)
India's recorded sex ratio (943) below biological norm — implies female under-registration + mortality
Missing women concept (Amartya Sen) — estimated 35-40 million missing women in India
Civil Registration System (CRS) vs Census enumeration — data source reliability for sex ratio

concepts.name: Census 2021 Postponement: Implications for Policy and Data Gaps
key_dimensions: Census 2021 delayed due to COVID — first time since 1871 a census was postponed in India
Policy vacuum: delimitation exercise, OBC sub-categorization, welfare scheme targeting all pending on census
Trap: All current policy uses 2011 data — candidates must not assume 2021 data is available
Caste census debate — its connection to census methodology and political implications

concepts.name: Density-Literacy-Sex Ratio Interrelationship: Integrated Analysis
key_dimensions: High density + low literacy + poor sex ratio = UP/Bihar model — demographic stress zones
Low density + high literacy + better sex ratio = Kerala/NE model — sustainability zones
Trap: Punjab has high literacy + high density but worst CSR — prosperity-equity disconnect
UPSC GS1 integrative questions linking all three parameters to development outcomes and policy

concepts.name: Worker Population Ratio and Its Linkage to Literacy and Urbanisation
key_dimensions: Total workers (2011): 39.8% of population — main workers vs marginal workers distinction
Female Work Participation Rate (FWPR): 25.5% vs male 53.3% — literacy correlation
Trap: High female literacy in Kerala but low FWPR — educated unemployment paradox
Urban FWPR vs Rural FWPR — rural women more in agriculture (counted) vs urban women in informal sector (undercounted)
